title: Three things we
noticed about Open Studio
Three things
we noticed
about Open Studio
sections.kicker: Prepared for Open Studio by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Open Studio says it lets everything in, and a studio that welcomes everything has not chosen anything.
sections.keep: The two filled circles in the wordmark. They are a simple and ownable idea.

pins.what: The intro lists ideas, perspectives and possibilities.
pins.why: Saying yes to everything is the opposite of a position, and it leaves a client with no reason to pick this studio.
pins.how: Say what Open Studio turns down and what it does better than anyone.
pins.label: Your intro
pins.cost: Every studio that welcomes ideas sounds the same, so Open Studio competes on being friendly.

pins.what: The sentence ends on a promise of something extraordinary.
pins.why: Every studio says the same, and the line offers no sign of what that thing looks like.
pins.how: Replace it with one specific result.
pins.label: Your intro
pins.cost: A claim that anyone can make cannot be remembered.

pins.area: The word OPEN STUDIO with a solid white circle in place of each O over black and white footage
pins.what: The O at each end of the name is a filled circle over blurred black and white footage of a glass door.
pins.why: The circle is the one distinctive mark, and the footage does not show anything the studio has made.
pins.how: Let the circle carry the identity and put real work behind it.
pins.label: Your wordmark
pins.cost: The idea that could be theirs is used as decoration over footage.

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on Open Studio's own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
sections.note: A few short questions first, then you pick a time. You can also just reply to the email.
